result:
PR #383 is now marked ready. The re-registered prediction passes on the device: all 291 checks hold. The PR still carries the `regressed` label, though, and it should clear once the host's arms job judges the second arm.

**Why the last attempt stalled:** the second arm finished on the device (Nova), but the arms job never judged it. The only `[job.arms]` verdict posted was for the old, superseded prediction against the first arm, and that is where the `regressed` label came from. I judged the second arm myself with `ab_compare.py` against the prediction file the host had locked when it queued the arm. The lane can't write the host's verdict files, so the label stays until the arms job catches up.

**Arm 2 result:**
- 295 of 300 captures are unchanged.
- The 5 that moved are all `Vertex_shader_rounding_tests/GeometrySuperscreen_*`, which the prediction deliberately leaves unchecked. 4 got better and 1 got worse.
- That suite is unstable on its own: the two base runs of the same master build came out different from each other.
- `GeometrySuperscreen_0.5000` went off in both fix runs and in neither base run. It also went off in two older base runs (the vshnobegin242 arms on Thor) that don't carry this change. The change only acts when a dot product is already NaN, and that test has no inf/NaN inputs, so I don't count 2 of 2 as a real effect.

**Definition of done:**
- Preflight passes on the new head `a5722d6813`, with `--allow-tracker`.
- The branch merges cleanly into master. Master hasn't touched `vsh-prog.c` since the branch point, so I made no merge and the prediction's refs stay as they were.
- The PR's `Files:` line matches the diff. I updated it over REST and read it back.
- `docs/lanes/dpforce345/NOTES.md` covers the arm 2 result and why attempt 2 didn't finish. The verdict output and the hash comparison are committed next to it. Both were gitignored, so I force-added them.
- A `[lane.dpforce345] done:` comment on the PR cites the verdict.

CI on the new head hadn't been checked when this session ended.

The fixed evaluator for the console's CPU Shader Tests (half 2 of #345) is not built. NOTES.md explains why it isn't a small fix and leaves it to the board as a follow-up.
